title: secp256k1 v26: success floor WITHDRAWN and disclosed -- direct counts d=0 467/1200 (CP95 0.365819), d=4 190/1200, d=16 0/1200, no transfer, no ratio, no pooling; work bound stands at 128.533 with sigma beta^h + mod-r reductions priced (754 insn); key-level detector, 36-pair adversarial set

claims.statement: On secp256k1-ecdlp this package claims the COMPUTATION BOUND W = 2^128.533 (reduced rational 128533/1000) for the shipped DP-walk configuration (2^20 lanes, inversion BATCH 2^18, production DP density d=60, step 754 itemised instructions at C=1000, w=2 exactly +1.000 bit). THE SUCCESS FLOOR IS WITHDRAWN AND DISCLOSED, NOT TRANSFERRED. This package does NOT claim recovery probability >= 0.390 at production DP density: that floor is WITHDRAWN and the claim is the work bound alone. WHY, in the words of the re-judged flaw: the success row must be a DIRECTLY COUNTED recovery event (the walk decodes xx and [xx]G == Q), and the CP lower bound must come from THAT count alone, in one cell, with no multiplicative correction and no pooling. Measured, n=1200 per cell, 2^17 classes, L=16, R=32, production class key, lag-3 escape: d=0 467/1200 = 0.389167 (CP95 0.365819); d=4 190/1200 = 0.158333 (CP95 0.141217); d=8 14/1200 = 0.011667 (CP95 0.007067); d=12 1/1200 = 0.000833 (CP95 0.000043); d=16 0/1200 = 0.000000 (CP95 0.000000). The best measured cell is d=0 at 0.365818960 CP-95, which is BELOW 0.390, and the direct count collapses with the gate density the way the production gate requires: by d=16 it is 0/1200. Production runs at d=60. NO cell therefore supports a production success floor, and none is asserted. WHAT WAS DELETED, and why. (1) The exp-of-mean substitution: f(T)=(1-p)^T is convex, so E[(1-p)**T] >= (1-p)**E[T] and the v24 number was an upper bound on success, not the success. (2) The exact-sum ratio correction R: its T was total visits across ALL lanes before the first solve or budget exhaustion, a STOPPING TIME, and 1/mean(T) is not the DP density 2**-60 -- that statistic did not measure the recovery event and could not be rescaled into one, so R is withdrawn rather than repaired. (3) The bootstrap interval and the pooled 3600-trial CP bound: pooling cells is forbidden by the earlier verdict and the bootstrap is not a production bound. (4) 'trail/2'. Nothing in this package transfers a rate between cells, orders, densities or lane counts. WHAT SURVIVES. The deterministic work bound: every instruction the walk can execute is a charged row, so realized work <= W by construction, and W is priced at 754 instructions per step after two previously unpriced rows were added -- sigma's beta^h application gets its own full F_p multiply (97) plus a 512->256 reduction mod p (97), because the selector's partial-product window is the selector's input and not its result, and the mu6 rescale gets a separate reduction row of 2 x 97 for reducing the full 512-bit product mod r instead of counting only 16 schoolbook mul-adds and one conditional subtract. That moves the claim from 128.172 to 128.533 (+0.361 bits): the work bound got WORSE and it is the tested algorithm's own price. The class key is compared KEY-to-KEY between two independent implementations over the whole adversarial set. Every literal here is generated by scripts/regen_v26.py from evidence/ledger-v26.json. NOT RANKING: the claim is 2.195 bits above the live bar 126.338.
